data.title: QNT surges 38% as Quant’s institutional adoption deepens – 3 signals to watch
data.description:
Quant ecosystem entered a stronger market phase after institutional developments extended its role across regulated tokenized payment infrastructure in key financial markets.

Recently, Quant was selected by the Clearing House for its On-Chain Money Initiative before the token’s recent rally unfolded. Reportedly, the network handles approximately $2 trillion in daily U.S. payments.

Additionally, U.K. banks also completed live customer transactions, including tokenized sterling deposits through Quant’s ecosystem. These developments combined reinforced Quant’s institutional adoption picture before investors repriced QNT aggressively.

Subsequently, the token rallied 38%, while its spot trading volume climbed 228.9% to nearly $38.2 million. Similar activity was also reflected in the derivatives markets, where leverage accelerated much faster.

Fresh leverage floods into QNT

In particular, the derivatives participants drastically increased their exposure as QNT price pushed higher alongside the growing spot participation.

Furthermore, the corresponding derivatives volume also climbed 637.49% to $214.37 million, considerably exceeding the expansion recorded across the spot markets. 

Notably, QNT’s Open Interest also pumped 78.87% to $29.54 million as investors opened fresh leveraged positions.

The overall Long/Short Ratio stood at 1.0483, leaving the positioning slightly tilted towards the longs. 

Additionally, the liquidations, however, revealed greater pressure on market participants betting against the rally.

Specifically, the short liquidations hit $439.43K during 24 hours, with only $65.67K across the long positions. The forced short closures therefore likely amplified buying during QNT’s sharp price rally.

However, this derivatives expansion also elevated QNT’s sensitivity to sudden price swings. 

Spot demand meets growing supply pressure

The Spot Taker CVD remained buyer-dominant as the aggressive buyers continued protecting QNT price advance. 

On the other hand, the futures Taker CVD remained seller-dominant, implying resistance from the leveraged market participants.

Therefore, this divergence separated the underlying spot demand from the more cautious positioning visible across the futures markets.

The exchange reserves meanwhile jumped 39.49% to nearly $112 million in 24 hours, placing considerably more QNT within exchange wallets as the rally unfolded.

The higher exchange reserves introduced a potential sell-side supply in case holders move tokens onto exchanges for distribution. However, the buyer-dominant spot activity had absorbed pressure as QNT price pushed higher.

Eventually, sustaining the demand could become crucial as price approaches a major technical barrier.

Can QNT clear its next barrier?

The weekly technical price structure changed considerably following the recent price advance. 

On the charts, Quant [QNT] broke above its prolonged descending channel, reclaiming the $80.53 price level. This breakout marked an important shift from its previous weekly structure.

Subsequently, the price surged towards the $102.91 resistance area, with QNT reaching $98.65 at the time of the press. 

Notably, the RSI indicator rose to 68.16 during the breakout, approaching overbought territory but not yet crossing the 70 threshold.

Additionally, the directional positioning also changed sharply with DMI showing the +DI signal at 35.29, substantially above the -DI signal at 13.63.

The ADX indicator, however, remained lower at 12.73, leaving room for a stronger trend confirmation despite the broadening directional gap. 

Therefore, the $102.91 price level became the next test for buyers following the channel breakout.

Ultimately, a strong breakout could expose the $131.77 level as the next key resistance while a rejection could return QNT towards $80.53 support for a breakout retest.

Final Summary

  • Institutional payment adoption provided QNT’s catalyst, while spot buyers supported the resulting rally.
  • Rising exchange reserves and futures selling could challenge QNT’s breakout near $102.91.

data.title: EU targets $54B DeFi sector as Aave slams Morpho’s vault proposal as ‘self-serving’
data.description:
The European Union [EU] wants to bring crypto lending within the scope of the MiCA framework. In a recent policy review, the European Banking Authority (EBA) said that DeFi lending and borrowing should be regulated. 

EBA crafts policy and regulates the EU-wide banking sector to ensure financial stability and user protection. 

According to EBA, crypto lending, either via an intermediated interface of crypto asset service providers (CASPs) or DeFi protocols, can offer regulatory arbitrage for stablecoin yields.

MiCA banned stablecoin yield, but some, such as Circle’s USDC and EURC, still earn yield via DeFi strategies. For EBA, this could cause more problems, 

Thus, the activities (DeFi lending) may pose regulatory arbitrage risks. Additionally, the EBA and ESMA have identified a series of potential consumer protection risks.

The consumer protection risks highlighted by the watchdog include over-leverage, contagion risks, hacks, and fraud. 

To mitigate against these risks, EBA proposed a few considerations, including leverage caps, disclosure requirements, and cyber resilience-based certification for DeFi protocols.

Additionally, the proposed rules could bar unlicensed stablecoins such as USDT from DeFi lending. Regulators would likely focus on platforms that give users access to DeFi protocols through intermediated lending and borrowing.

The proposed EU approach differs from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission’s (SEC) approach. The SEC warned that securities laws could apply when curators actively manage vaults to generate yield. The treatment of fully non-custodial vaults remains less clear.

Still, leading industry players disagree on how regulators should classify on-chain vaults and which rules should apply.

Aave disagrees with Morpho on DeFi vaults

Vaults pool users’ assets and deploy them across lending opportunities. Some follow preset rules; others give curators discretion over where the assets go.

The segment held roughly $10 billion across more than 4,000 deployed vaults, within a $54 billion DeFi lending market.

However, Aave and Morpho, some of the top DeFi lending giants, are undecided on the classification of vaults for regulation.

Why did Aave challenge Morpho’s vault model?

For his part, Morpho CEO Paul Frambot proposed two categories: non-custodial and discretionary vaults. According to him, non-custodial vaults will limit curators’ role and allow user flexibility (including exit capacity or time lock).

In contrast, discretionary vaults should be managed by asset managers, but will trigger the SEC’s securities laws. 

However, Stani Kulechov discredited Frambot’s non-custodial vault proposal as weak. 

This categorisation doesn’t make sense and is pretty much self-serving. Vaults that could reasonably be considered non-custodial are those without a manager. There’s nothing inherently wrong with discretionary vaults, as long as the regulatory path is figured out.

Overall, the EU wants to expand MiCA oversight to crypto lending and borrowing, yet the industry is undecided on how to classify vaults. 

Final Summary

  • European banking regulator wants crypto lending to be regulated under MiCA with leverage caps and DeFi certification.
  • Aave’s Kulechov discredited Morpho’s proposed vault classification model for US regulation.

data.title: Bitget CEO confirms ‘loss containment’ after $352M hack: ‘Very likely a North Korean group’
data.description:
Bitget exchange CEO Gracy Chen has confirmed that the $351.6M loss has been contained, and that no further authorized transfers are possible. 

In an update on X, Chen said attackers had breached Bitget’s backend wallet infrastructure and fooled its authorization process. She said the exchange had since addressed that breach.

Private key compromise has been ruled out-this excludes the more severe risk scenarios. Loss containment is confirmed. No further unauthorized transfers are possible.

That distinction offered some relief. Stolen private keys could have given attackers continued control over the affected wallets. Still, Bitget had not set a date for restoring withdrawals.

Withdrawal restoration is being prepared in parallel. We will announce a timeline as soon as one is confirmed — we will not commit to a window we cannot guarantee.

Bitget hack update: $157M XRP lost amid Lazarus Group links

The security breach was first reported at 18:31 UTC on September 24. Out of the stolen assets, XRP accounted for nearly half of the heist at $157.4M. Ethereum [ETH], USDT, and USDC were also some of the top targeted assets, collectively accounting for +$140M of the stolen stash. 

Already, the attacker has begun swapping the funds into EVM chains via multiple wallets to obscure and launder them. So far, $163M has been swapped to ETH, according to on-chain data. 

Was the Bitget hack linked to Lazarus?

In her live update on X earlier, Chen said that the attack was likely carried out by a North Korean group, citing a key IP address pattern. 

We think it is very likely a North Korean group; it’s not internal. We’ve identified some IP addresses that match the VPN choices by a certain DPRK group.

Interestingly, Web3 security analyst Specter traced and linked the Bitget stolen XRP to the July AFX hack, which was carried out by the notorious Lazarus group. 

That said, the exchange had earlier stated that it has user protection funds that surpass $464M, noting that it is sufficient to cover the recent loss. 

In fact, even Bybit CEO Ben Zhou had reached out to offer help to their colleagues, including helping them track and tag the attackers’ wallets. In other words, users will likely be refunded fully. 

However, the incident is the second-largest centralized exchange breach after last year’s Bybit $1.5B breach. These high-value breaches are mainly handled by Lazarus Group.

But this further highlights how large centralized exchanges are increasingly being targeted by attackers, and calls for investor caution. 

Final Summary

  • Bitget CEO said there were no stolen private keys and confirmed the loss has been contained 
  • The $352M hack has been linked to the Lazarus Group, the attacker behind Bybit’s $1.5B breach

data.title: ‘Only hedge funds, retail sold’ — Will BTC sustain rally as Bitcoin ETF flows turn positive?
data.description:
U.S Spot Bitcoin ETFs have been on a winning streak for the past five days, effectively hauling in $2.65B in net inflows. 

The strong demand has flipped the ETF positive on a year-to-date (YTD) basis and lifted BTC’s price to an eight-month high of $87K. However, the bullish momentum is still facing renewed bond market pressure and a potential Fed rate hike in October. 

Can Bitcoin ETF demand survive macro pressure?

This week’s massive Spot BTC ETF demand turned YTD flows positive with $349M, according to Galaxy Research data.

On Monday alone, the ETF complex attracted $1B in daily inflows. On Tuesday, they hauled in another $714M, with these figures dropping slightly on Wednesday to $346M.

Overall, the ETF complex pulled in $2.65B. Out of the $2.65B demand seen over the past five days, BlackRock drove half of the ETF flows. 

In fact, even Bloomberg analyst James Seyffart noted that the recent traction could soon help the cumulative flows (aggregate demand since inception) turn positive too.

Since last October, the cumulative flows had dipped by $12B (77.8K BTC). However, the rebound has now erased it by half. The cumulative flows, or total BTC held by the ETF complex, were only down by 5.7% at press time. 

Here, it’s worth pointing out that Seyffart added that the outflows were mainly driven by hedge funds and retail.

By far, the biggest sellers of the ETFs over the last ~year were hedge funds and retail traders/investors.

The cumulative flows stood at $55B, despite the crypto winter. However, the institutional resilience and remarkable BTC ETF demand are being tested again by the bond market crisis and fears of another Fed rate hike. 

The bond yield jumped again to 5.1%, and oil prices also ticked slightly higher, reinforcing new inflation fears.

Similarly, interest rate traders seemed to be pricing a 64% chance of another hike during the next October Fed meeting. This dampened risk appetite mid-week and dragged BTC from $87K to below $84K on the charts.  

What’s next for Bitcoin?

In the past, U.S. Treasury intervention plans to control bond yields have been viewed as net inflationary and an overall boost to scarce assets such as BTC and gold. Whether that narrative will hold and drive BTC higher remains to be seen. 

For the rate hike fears, however, the asset typically remains muted before the Fed decision and tends to push higher afterwards. 

For his part, analyst Benjamin Cowen projected that the uptrend could only be confirmed if there is a weekly candlestick close above $82K (May peak). 

Final Summary

  • Bitcoin is facing double macro pressure from rising bond yields and Fed rate hike fears
  • Asset slipped by about 4% but could reinforce strength if it holds above the May peak of $82K

data.title: Why TRUMP crypto’s recovery odds depend on the $1.93 support
data.description:
As the  broader crypto market corrected, Official Trump [TRUMP] collapsed 11.28%  within 24 hours, while volume increased 15.47%, reflecting intensified participation throughout the selloff. The retracement pushed TRUMP’s market capitalization down to approximately $552.45 million.

The increase in spot volume to roughly $505 million suggested that the market participants remained actively involved as the memecoin extended its price fall. Such elevated volume also indicated substantial liquidity remained available as TRUMP approached an important technical price zone.

Eventually, TRUMP crypto‘s price stabilized around the $1.95 support zone, shifting attention towards whether sellers could force another breakdown.

Sellers control both Spot and Futures

According to CryptoQuant market indicators, selling activity pushed beyond price performance as the Taker CVD metric revealed pressure across both markets.

Notably, the Spot Taker CVD indicator preserved a seller dominance, implying aggressive sellers were still in control at the time of reporting. 

The futures Taker CVD signal also remained seller-dominant as the derivatives participants  maintained a similar pressure. This correlation, therefore, left the bulls without meaningful support from either side of the market.

Even so, the increasing volume indicated substantial participation continued despite the sharp price correction. However, buyers must counter this selling pressure before TRUMP crypto could establish a strong recovery.

Otherwise, the persistent taker selling could keep the memecoin compressed near support, threatening the broader technical price structure.

Can $1.93 preserve TRUMP’s pennant flag?

TRUMP crypto’s pullback brought the price toward the $1.93 level, where buyers had established support within the broader pennant structure, on the daily trading chart.

More importantly, the token remained inside the formation instead of confirming a breakdown beneath its lower boundary.

Additionally, the Parabolic SAR indicator sat around the $1.903 level at press time, placing the indicator beneath the prevailing price and also close to the same defensive region.

The RSI, on the other hand, retraced to 46.60, slipping below its moving average at 48.10. The technical indicator, however, remained comfortably above the oversold threshold despite the fading buying strength.

A successful hold of the $1.93 support could protect the pennant flag and support another attempt towards its descending upper boundary.

Subsequently, a strong breakout could bring the $2.30-price level into focus before TRUMP targets the larger $3.00-resistance zone. In contrast, losing the $1.93 key support, however, would weaken the setup and expose the lower $1.68 region.

Overhead liquidity offers a recovery incentive

The Binance Liquidation Heatmap provided another element as TRUMP defended its technical price structure.

Notably, dense liquidation concentration clusters developed above price around the $2.02 region and were also visible throughout the broader $2.05–$2.10 region.

These liquidity clusters could therefore likely attract the TRUMP price in case the bulls regain control from the aggressive bears. Besides, substantial liquidity, however, also remained beneath the prevailing market value around the $1.90–$1.93-area.

Therefore, TRUMP could likely sweep this lower liquidity before establishing a stronger price recovery from pennant support. Even so, holding the $1.93 support level would instead strengthen the path towards $2.02, followed by the broader overhead liquidity cluster.

Conclusively, TRUMP’s technical recovery structure remained intact above the $1.93 support, although the seller-dominant Taker CVD continued challenging buyers.

Ultimately, a sustained defense of the prevailing support could redirect price towards the overhead liquidity as $2.30 becomes the next major test.

Final Summary

  • TRUMP crypto held $1.93, keeping its broader pennant recovery structure intact.
  • Liquidity above $2 could support recovery, but taker sellers remained dominant.

data.title: Solana price tests $122 as new US stablecoin rules take shape
data.description:
Solana rose above the $119 price level after reaching an intraday high of $122.18, placing it near its strongest price level in months.

The move followed a proposal from the US Fed for further regulation of stable currency issuers. The recommendations will not directly regulate the Solana blockchain itself but can influence the functioning of digital dollars, controlled by the authorities via networks like Solana.

Federal Reserve proposes stablecoin safeguards

The Federal Reserve recently requested public comments on two proposals tied to the GENIUS Act.

One of the proposals requires that any stablecoin that comes under the supervision of the Fed should be 100% held against certain approved assets. One possible option for them is to be held up against short-term US treasury bills or some others that could easily be converted into cash.

The issuers would be required to possess the necessary capital capacity to take losses. Rules would extend from risk management to custody to their ability to allow their clients’ money to be returned when requested.

Another proposal would tell eligible banks and firms how they can get permission to issue stablecoins.

This move matters to Solana because stablecoins form part of both the large trading volume and payments that they host. Clear US regulations could attract regulated issuers and users to stablecoins for use on public blockchains.

The latest announcement does not mean that the Fed endorsed Solana or any other blockchain.

Solana faces its next test near $122

At the time of this writing, SOL was trading at around $119.51 after gaining 2.13%. During today’s trade, it reached highs of $122.18 before cooling down.

Buyers seem to remain in control following the price climb from below the $100 price level earlier in September. With the latest move also came increased trading activity, giving the recovery some support.

The immediate hurdle sits between the $122 and $124 price levels. SOL has entered that region, but it has not yet established itself above it.

A convincing move beyond $124 could allow for further gains. If buyers can’t keep up, the $116 price level is the first level to watch. A deeper pullback could bring the price towards the $108–$110 region, where buyers previously stepped in.

Final Summary

  • The Federal Reserve has some proposals for stablecoin issuers.
  • SOL reached the $122.18 price level, but it must move beyond the $124 level to strengthen its latest breakout.

data.title: Tezos launches Quantumnet – Inside its early quantum-defense plan
data.description:
Future quantum computers are acting as a threat to the current blockchain technology, which relies heavily on cryptography such as elliptic-curve signatures.

Hence, to protect itself from this threat, Tezos has launched Quantumnet, an experimental test network. However, it is not the final post-quantum version of Tezos or ready for production use.

Instead, it is a testing ground where the developers can identify problems, measure performance, and refine the technology before potentially proposing it as a future protocol amendment.

Tezos plays the test match

In an email to AMBCrypto, Zaynah Dargaye, Core Layer 1 Engineering Manager at Nomadic Labs, said,

Quantumnet gives us a space to experiment rigorously and in the open on a major topic for the Tezos ecosystem.

He added,

We are doing this work early so that we have the time to learn, iterate and ultimately make sure Tezos is ready for a post-quantum future, with as smooth a transition path as possible. This is just the beginning, and it is particularly exciting to see this work taking shape.

So for now, Tezos is testing quantum-resistant cryptography across multiple layers of its blockchain, and not just user accounts.

Quantumnet uses ML-DSA-44 for tz5 account signatures and Smooth Weighted Round Robin for baker selection. It also tests post-quantum signature aggregation for consensus and ZODA for data availability.

Meanwhile, TzEL is exploring confidential post-quantum transactions separately. That leaves Tezos with several pieces to test together before any change reaches its live network.

Blockchain prepares against quantum threats

This coincided with Ethereum developers targeting the end of 2029 to make L1 quantum-resistant. They planned an intermediate step for late 2026.

At the same time, Bitcoin’s quantum defense has already taken a step forward after StarkWare and the MARA Foundation conducted the first known quantum-resistant Bitcoin transaction on the 27th of August.

Final Summary

  • Quantumnet is not the final post-quantum version of Tezos.
  • Tezos is testing quantum-resistant cryptography across multiple layers of its blockchain.

data.title: SEI crypto jumps 38%– THESE 2 key targets are now in focus
data.description:
Sei [SEI] rallied 9.2% in 24 hours while Bitcoin [BTC] consolidated near $84,000. Bitcoin had retreated from $87,300 earlier in the week, with $81,000 a possible downside level.

The broader crypto market cap slipped 0.20%, but Sei bulls held their ground. Earlier this week, they flipped the late-June supply zone near $0.055 into support.

SEI crypto appeared likely to rally higher, especially after the Canary staked ETF filing.

Can Sei break its weekly downtrend?

The weekly chart showed that the long-term Sei crypto token trend was firmly bearish. However, over the past six weeks, trading volume has begun to pick up after the June-July consolidation around $0.045.

The rising volume was accompanied by upward momentum and price gains, which indicated demand. The MFI was climbing but not yet above neutral 50 to signal that buyers have the upper hand.

A weekly session close above $0.080 is needed to signal that a potential bullish trend shift is underway.

On the daily timeframe, the $0.055-$0.060 bearish order block has been cleared. Additionally, the swing structure on this timeframe was also flipped bullishly since the previous lower high just under $0.060 was beaten.

The OBV has climbed to highs not seen since January. The MFI was in overbought territory, showing that bulls had the upper hand in recent weeks.

Traders’ call to action- Look to buy

The 4-hour chart showed that a bullish continuation signal was once again upon us. After SEI crypto retraced into the $0.055 demand zone, it has reacted positively to challenge the $0.0646 local high.

An H4 session close above this level would mean the $0.072 level is a feasible target in the coming days. In that scenario, the $0.0568 low would be the one to watch to keep this timeframe’s uptrend intact.

Final Summary

  • SEI crypto has surpassed local swing resistance levels and was on a healthy uptrend, up 9% in a day and 38% in a week.
  • Its higher timeframe trend has been bearish, and a move above $0.080 would be the first sign of a potential long-term recovery.

data.title: Pi Network: Will mainnet KYC upgrades save PI crypto from drop to $0.076?
data.description:
Pi Network [PI] was down 2.35% in 24 hours.

Since last Tuesday, the 15th of September, the altcoin has been laboring under a bearish short-term trend. It managed to bounce to $0.0948 by the 22nd of September, but has fallen 9.37% in the three days since.

In other news, the Pi Network team released technical updates related to KYC and mainnet migration processes. They address specific KYC application corner cases, improve verification processes, and expand device eligibility for liveness checks, among other things.

PI crypto stuck within a bearish long-term structure

On the 1-day timeframe, the prevalent swing structure (white) was bearish. Within this structure, PI crypto formerly appeared to form a higher low at $0.0844 (green) in August, and pushed higher to $0.1108.

This push was brief and faltered almost immediately. Moreover, the price failed to close a daily candle above the $0.10 psychological zone and local supply.

These factors indicated weakness from buyers, a view vindicated when PI crypto slipped below the $0.0844 local support. This move flipped the internal structure bearishly.

The OBV has been relatively flat over the past two months, when Pi Network token oscillated about the $0.08-$0.10 area. The Awesome Oscillator also remained muted in recent weeks, but took a bearish turn a week ago.

Traders’ call to action- Sell

On the 4-hour timeframe, the internal structure shift on the daily appeared as a swing structure shift. Since this bearish shift a week ago, the PI crypto price bounced almost exactly to the 78.6% Fibonacci retracement level at $0.0984.

The altcoin witnessed a bearish reaction from this key retracement level, showing that the short-term trend was bearish.

Therefore, traders and investors can expect further price decline. To the south, the 23.6% extension level at $0.07595 is the next target for PI crypto.

The $0.0703 low, made in July, was another key support level to watch. A price drop below this level would signal a higher-timeframe bearish trend continuation.

Final Summary

  • PI crypto has a bearish long-term price structure that was reinforced by its rejection from the $0.10 round-number resistance.
  • A price decline to $0.076 and $0.070 appeared likely in the coming days and weeks.

data.title: Assessing Litecoin’s latest price breakout after bulls clear major $60.61 swing high
data.description:
Litecoin [LTC] was one of the top-20 crypto assets by market capitalization to record a sizeable price gain in the last 24 hours. While many altcoins, including LTC, saw double-digit returns over the past week, most were affected by Bitcoin’s [BTC] pullback from $87.3K to $82.9K by Thursday, 24th September.

At the time of writing, LTC bulls had noted gains of 6.04% in just 24 hours. On the weekly charts too, the altcoin was up by 29.2%, with the altcoin having breached its significant resistance at $60.

A closer look at Litecoin’s long-term trends

The Fixed Range Volume Profile was used to plot the volume profile from January’s high to the present day. It showed that the VAH (dotted blue) was at $60.50, a key swing level.

On the weekly chart, the Awesome Oscillator made a bullish crossover above the zero line, the first time the indicator flashed positive readings on this timeframe since October 2025.

The price also pierced the swing high at $60.61 made in May, flipping its weekly structure bullishly. The Directional Movement Index highlighted a strong uptrend in progress on the weekly timeframe.

Meanwhile, the OBV was still languishing near its multi-month lows stretching back to March. The weekly trading volume has not been explosive despite the bullish breakout. It could be a warning of weak buyer strength behind the move.

Despite the volume warning, however, Litecoin still maintains a bullish bias in the higher timeframes due to its rally past $60.

Traders’ call to action – Buy the pullback

On the daily timeframe, the OBV made new highs and seemed to be far more encouraging. Other technical indicators also supported a bullish view. The price structure was also firmly bullish.

A pullback would offer a buying opportunity, given the trends across the daily and weekly timeframes.

The $60 and $52.50-levels are the key demand zones to watch out for on the daily chart. Swing traders and investors can wait for a bullish reaction from these areas to consider going long on Litecoin.

Final Summary

  • Litecoin’s price rally past $60.61 marked a higher timeframe trend shift.
  • A pullback towards $60 or $52 could offer swing traders and investors a chance to buy.
